Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to get a sense of Avery's latency targets and the compliance questions around data residency. Quick recap:

- Primary goal: host inference in your VPC (AWS account) with customer-managed KMS and audit logs forwarded to your Splunk instance.
- Target P95 latency: <= 120ms for text generation at 1k tokens/session.
- Expected steady throughput: ~40 concurrent users, occasional spikes for monthly batch scoring.
- Primary constraints: air-gapped approval path for PHI workflows and SOC2 evidence for audit.

We recommend a two-part next session: 1) an architecture deep-dive with our SE to validate network/topology and KMS integration; 2) a short admin walkthrough on the private control plane and audit exports. Connor (copied) can lead the first; Vivek will cover procurement and SOW questions.

Can you confirm availability for a 60-minute architecture review? Slots we have open next week (PST):
- Tue 2026-12-07 10:00–11:00
- Wed 2026-12-08 14:00–15:00
- Thu 2026-12-09 08:30–09:30

If none of those work, send a couple of preferred windows and we'll align. Also, could you loop in the person who owns KMS/audit (you mentioned Nina) so we can cover key material?

Attached: redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf — a short questionnaire that helps our SE prepare (network ports, CIDR, expected request profiles). I also included a one-page list of pre-demo questions to save time.

Thanks — talk soon,

—Stephanie

Hi Jordan / team — Connor from Redwood SE here. Confirming I'll lead the infra deep-dive on Dec 8. I see the checklist — thanks for filling that out in advance if you can. Quick notes on your questions:

- KV cache: We can scope KV/cache persistence to the instance storage in your VPC; there are also options for ephemeral caches vs. durable object stores depending on your availability profile. I'll prepare two diagrams (ephemeral-cache flow vs. durable-KV flow) and bring them to the session.
- Audit logs: We typically stream structured JSON events (timestamp, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, user_id_hash) to S3 or directly to a SIEM via a forwarding connector. Retention policies are customer-configurable; default on Redwood Private is 90 days, with options for 1yr/indefinite depending on subscription.

I've created a tentative calendar event: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-avery-arch-review — please accept if the time works. I've attached a short slide with the two cache topology options.
